questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Agricultural systems and soil science brought everything together i learned so far and made everything make sense to me. 
Laboratory in sustainability of water management was a very in depth and practical course with a lot of theory and a very challenging group project
REMOTE SENSING OF AGRO-ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE very well thaught course that helps understand all the basics of remote sensing and builds from there to also understand more complex problems, use remote sensing and understand its future uses. good combination of one very passionate yet pacient teacher and some guest lectures on very cool topics.

questions.answer: costs for futsal team, i played in an official team with extra costs for health checks and uniforms. also health check to be allowed to run marathon. health check is expensive, event specific, and almost always required when participating in sport events

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing futsal team

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: futsal team at university (also other sports, but all with selection procedure). didnt participate in other activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: teamsports!!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: hike in the mountains!!!! or visit nice neighbouring cities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, people were very kind and italy has a good lifestyle :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: teamsports!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the language barrier, many girls in my team didnt speak english, but with mutual effort everything worked out fine. also bureaucracy at uni sometimes got to much for me to understand and i couldnt really find coherent documents or websites explaining administrative things

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the warmth and welcomeness, the people, the time they take for coffee and food, the way teachers are always willing to take time and help

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
enjoy the italian lifestyle
dare to ask for help, and do it soon before bureaucratic stuff gets more and more
try to learn the language (already a bit in advance)
go fore hikes!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: there is a youth travel card for 22 euros per month through atm which i would really recommend

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to enjoy the opportunities milan has with amazing people from different cultures. also worked on an amazing project for my thesis with very knowledgeble people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: bureaucracy
